newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan retailers' rating outlook stable - Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Japan retailers' rating outlook stable - Moody's.

text.p: Despite a weak operating environment and other difficulties, the overall rating outlook for Japanese retailers is stable, Moody's Investors Service Inc said on Monday.

"Japanese retailers' ratings already incorporate the weak retailing environment and selective consumer spending that are expected to pressure their cash flow and debt-servicing capability," Moody's said in its report.
Moody's currently rates one trillion yen worth of long-term debt issued by 10 major Japanese retailers, including Daiei Inc and Isetan Co Ltd.
"Japanese retailers continue to face a challenging economic environment as low economic growth and high unemployment have resulted in weak consumer spending," the report said.
The report said that changing lifestyles and consumption patterns had given superstores and discounters a competitive edge against department stores.
But the report also said that the threat to traditional retailers was limited to some extent as segmentation of merchandise by distribution channel was continuing.
